standard_prerequisites: The Powersets axiom: for every set A the set of all subsets of A exists.
The Separation scheme: for every set A and formula phi, the set of elements of A satisfying phi exists.

The ordered pair construction and its existence properties from the pairs-consequences proposition of the same unit: for any sets x and y the pair {x} and {x, y} and the ordered pair (x, y) exist; published as corpus card X2-logic-z-singleton-binunion-pairs.

The Kuratowski encoding of the ordered pair (x, y) as the set with elements {x} and {x, y}, so that (x, y) is an element of the powerset of the powerset of A union B whenever x and y lie in A union B.
core_obligations: Show the two-fold powerset exists: since A union B exists, applying Powersets twice gives the set of all subsets of the set of all subsets of A union B.
Apply Separation inside that two-fold powerset to carve out C, the set of exactly those elements that are ordered pairs (x, y) with x in A and y in B.

Verify the encoding: for x in A and y in B the ordered pair exists by the pairs-consequences proposition, and since x, y lie in A union B the singletons {x} and {x, y} lie in the powerset of A union B, so (x, y) lies in the two-fold powerset, i.e., in C.
Conclude that C contains exactly the ordered pairs with first coordinate in A and second in B, so the Cartesian product A times B exists and equals C.
proof_roadmap: Composition construction: two-fold Powersets supplies the ambient set, Separation carves out the pair-containing subset, and the membership check is a two-line unpacking of the Kuratowski encoding against the pairs-consequences proposition; equality of A times B with C is then immediate.
difficulty_reason: A composition construction whose care points are the correct ambient set (two-fold powerset of the union) and the membership unpacking showing each ordered pair lands in it; both directions of the equality with C must be checked.
